subject: BlueHarbor: hosting posture decision ladder — private vs. dedicated sizing
messages:

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: BlueHarbor: hosting posture decision ladder — private vs. dedicated sizing

Hi Samira —

Great to meet last week. Per our conversation I put together a short decision ladder to help BlueHarbor choose between Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and a Private deployment (VPC / customer-managed). The goal: quantify the GPU footprint and gating security artifacts we need to land an initial pilot and next-quarter commit.

High-level ask from you: can you confirm expected steady-state queries-per-second (QPS) and 95th-percentile prompt length for the pilot workload? Two quick scenarios below we can tune once we have those numbers.

Scenario assumptions (initial):
- Model: open-Llama-family equivalent, quantized 8-bit runtime profile
- Typical request: 2.5 prompts / session, average 600 tokens per request (prompt+response)
- Target P95 latency: < 500ms for single-request interactive paths
- Concurrency target: pilot 50 concurrent sessions; ramp to 250 in committed phase

Preliminary sizing (very rough):
- Dedicated reserve: 6 x A100-40GB (baseline) -> handles ~200 QPS steady with burst headroom; includes 20% spare capacity for canary/failover
- Private (VPC/on-prem) air-gapped option: 8 x A100-40GB due to higher replication and reduced multi-tenant batching gains; add +2 GPUs for redundancy and faster KV warm cache

Compliance notes: SOC2 evidence, KMS integration, and audit logs are feasible in both modes; Private will need network segmentation and on-prem provisioning lead time (6–8 weeks).

If you can share the pilot QPS and procurement window I’ll convert these into a committed capacity ask and a mutually actionable rollout plan. I attached a short workbook with the assumptions (blueharbor_capacity_workbook.xlsx).

Thanks —
Jonas

Jonas, thanks — this is helpful. Couple of clarifying questions before we move to numbers: 

1) For the Private option, can you outline the minimum SOC2 controls you would need us to evidence before we can go live? Procurement is going to push hard on that list.
2) Cost delta: can you ballpark monthly run-rate delta between 6x and 8x A100 (we will need a headline for executive review)?
3) What does failover look like if we route to Dedicated from Private in the event of an incident?

Pilot target: roughly 40 concurrent active agents initially; expected steady QPS ~35 (bursty), with a projected commit to 200 concurrent agents if pilot metrics are met. Pilot window target: early Jan 2027.

If you can return a short exec note and a minimal evidence checklist that would speed procurement.

Subject: Fwd: BlueHarbor: hosting posture decision ladder — need quick sizing and compliance checklist

Marissa / Evelyn —

Forwarding Samira's questions. Pilot data: 35 QPS bursty, 40 concurrent agents initial, target commit -> 200 concurrent. Procurement wants SOC2 checklist + an exec-level cost delta. Can you validate the GPU math below and confirm recommended buffer for P95 latency?

My quick calc (feel free to correct):
- Baseline throughput per A100-40GB (quantized 8-bit, optimized kernels): ~1.2 tokens/ms sustained for the family we're targeting. Effective tokens/sec ~1200 tokens/s per GPU under mixed traffic.
- With 600 tokens/request average -> roughly 2.0 requests/sec per GPU (1200 / 600).
- For 35 QPS steady: we need ~18 GPUs raw (35 / 2.0 = 17.5) — this is because requests are larger than microbenchmarks; however, continuous batching in Dedicated reduces effective token cost per request by ~25% for multi-tenant pooling.

Deducting batching gains (Dedicated):
- Effective requests/sec per GPU becomes ~2.5 -> 35 QPS / 2.5 = 14 GPUs -> plus 2 GPUs for headroom = 16 GPUs -> map to a small dedicated pool (16 x A100) for pilot headroom and some burst.

Private (isolated):
- No multi-tenant batching gains and need extra replicas for isolation and KV-warm redundancy -> assume 30% higher GPU requirement -> 16 * 1.3 ≈ 21 GPUs -> recommend 22 GPUs (round up) for pilot in Private mode.

Notes on SLA/failover:
- Routed failover from Private -> Dedicated: we can configure read-only fallback (no writes to customer-managed KV) and model-variant fallback to a slightly smaller quantized profile for capacity easing; recovery RTO target 15–30 mins depending on cache warm-up.

I'll attach a quick workbook with simulation tabs and a one-pager SOC2 evidence summary for procurement (SOC2_evidence_summary.pdf). Marissa: can you add cost delta for 16 vs 22 A100 monthly (run-rate + 12-month committed pricing)?

-Jonas

Samira —

Attached are the two files we discussed: blueharbor_capacity_workbook.xlsx (sizing scenarios and simulation tabs) and SOC2_evidence_summary.pdf (minimal evidence checklist for procurement). Executive summary below for your review and quick presentation to leadership: 

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
BlueHarbor can run a low-latency pilot with either Redwood Dedicated (reserved multi-tenant GPU pools) or a Private VPC deployment. For the pilot profile you shared (35 QPS bursty, 40 concurrent agents -> commit to 200), our recommendations are: Dedicated: 16 x A100-40GB (lower unit run-rate due to batching and shared KV caches) vs Private: 22 x A100-40GB (higher footprint to preserve isolation and warm caches). The Private option adds ~35–40% to the monthly GPU run-rate but reduces shared-blast surface and satisfies stricter network controls; provisioning lead time for Private is ~6–8 weeks. Failover from Private to Dedicated is supported with a 15–30 minute cache warm-up window and an automatic model-variant fallback to mitigate capacity spikes.

Action items / next steps:
- Samira: confirm pilot procurement window (target early Jan 2027) and authorized point of contact for SOC2 evidence exchange.
- Procurement: review SOC2_evidence_summary.pdf and indicate any additional evidence needs.
- Marissa / Evelyn: finalize committed pricing delta for 16 vs 22 A100 monthly and produce a short slide for execs.

Links / attachments: blueharbor_capacity_workbook.xlsx (drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-blueharbor-capacity), SOC2_evidence_summary.pdf

Thanks everyone — we can run a 30-minute sync next week to close on procurement asks.

Best,
Jonas
